purpose: localize the nonlinear id bottleneck; two candidate fixes TESTED and both REFUTED by measurement

hypothesis_1_skeleton_proposer.verdict: REFUTED — precision-matrix skeleton proposer WORKS on tanh (truth_in_pool 0.917, HIGHER than linear). Truth is reachable; the bottleneck is downstream RESOLUTION.

hypothesis_2_saturation_smaller_interven.verdict: REFUTED (opposite) — SMALLER do-values give WORSE id. Larger interventions create larger between-structure prediction differences -> better discrimination. Nonlinear id is NOT saturation-limited fixable by smaller C.

honest_state: nonlinear DISCOVERY gap is real and OPEN: truth reachable (0.917), discrimination improves with LARGER interventions, organ swap fixes PREDICTION (err 0.454->0.279, advantage +0.174) but not DISCOVERY (id ~0.17-0.33, noisy at n=5/12-domains). Remaining candidates NOT yet tested: mean-field do-propagation inaccuracy (E[f(X)]!=f(E[X])), and minimality breakdown under nonlinearity (spurious edges get small-but-nonzero basis weights, so 'truth=unique minimal' may not hold). Requires a fresh, careful measurement pass — not more end-of-context guessing.
id_estimate_noise_caveat: id at n=5/12-domains is noisy (do-sampling randomness gave 0.167 vs 0.333 for the same tanh+nonlinear-organ config across two runs); qualitative conclusion (nonlinear id << linear 0.83; organ swap doesn't fix discovery; smaller C worse) is robust, point estimates are not.
